A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VQEL research despite changes to the title and presentation. All 17 pages of each version, including equations, figures and tables, support comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A and B.

before.justification: V1 reports original referential-game experiments on Synthetic Objects, dSprites and CelebA, including performance comparisons and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments on four datasets, including self-play variants, a no-self-play control and the additional experiments in Appendices A and B.

M1.justification: The core three-module VQ architecture remains, but v2 introduces substantive training variants: freezing the sender, combining reinforcement learning with a language-preserving self-play objective, and pretraining the receiver or both agents. Section 4.4 also specifies cosine codebook matching for the main experiments, whereas v1 specifies Euclidean matching. These extend the procedure beyond the original self-play followed by sender reinforcement learning.

E1.justification: V2 retains Synthetic Objects, dSprites and CelebA and adds ShapeWorld, including evaluation on held-out color-shape combinations. This is a focused extension of synthetic visual and compositional coverage within the retained referential-game task.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates only REINFORCE as an external baseline, although it discusses Gumbel-Softmax. V2 actually evaluates straight-through Gumbel-Softmax with learned temperature alongside REINFORCE throughout Tables 1–5. Adding this central alternative substantially strengthens the comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds active vocabulary fraction, topographic similarity and conditional concept entropy to the evaluation. It retains only vocabulary size 10 and message length 4, removing the smaller-channel setting, and changes candidate-count evaluations from the original table settings to curves spanning 2–512 candidates. The stated fixed sampling temperature becomes a searched parameter, and new freezing and no-self-play controls expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of self-play versus VQ architecture alone (Table 3), sender update and agent-role comparisons, and cosine-versus-Euclidean analysis (Appendix A). Appendix B investigates receiver-only pretraining and its failure. Conversely, v1's commitment-weight, message-length and vocabulary-size sensitivity studies in Figures 4–6 are removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report values with ± terms, but v2's candidate-count curves omit the uncertainty previously shown alongside candidate-count accuracies in v1's tables. V1's explicit mean-and-standard-deviation sensitivity plots also disappear. V2 mentions different seeds for initializing the two agents, which does not establish additional repetitions; neither version specifies repeat counts.

E6.justification: Results are substantially replaced and expanded. For CelebA with 100 candidates, v1 Table 3 reports 67.6% for VQEL after mutual play versus 58.2% for REINFORCE; v2 Table 1 reports 0.91 for sender-pretrained VQEL with RL versus 0.93 for REINFORCE, while both-agent pretraining reaches 0.94 in Table 2. These are revised settings and variants, not established same-setting gains. New metric and ablation results accompany removal of the smaller-channel and sensitivity results.

T1.justification: V2 adds the mathematical definition of the GS-ST baseline's learned inverse temperature (Equation 9) and explicitly specifies reward as negative receiver contrastive loss, where v1 leaves the loss-or-accuracy reward ambiguous. The core VQ and contrastive-loss mathematics is otherwise largely equivalent and reorganized; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central VQ-based self-play contribution remains. However, v2's conclusion adds substantive claims that self-play itself drives the gains beyond the VQ architecture, that VQEL achieves complete vocabulary use and lower concept-message entropy, and that performance compares favorably with both REINFORCE and Gumbel-Softmax. V1 primarily claimed REINFORCE superiority, controllability and reduced collapse without isolating self-play's contribution.

C2.justification: V1's explanations connecting commitment weight and channel capacity to exploration difficulties are removed. V2 introduces explanations based on sender codebook initialization, attributes the CelebA sender-only shortfall to the frozen pretrained encoder, and identifies receiver-only pretraining as a failure condition in Appendix B. It also qualifies the relationship between communication accuracy and topographic similarity.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies GRUs, baseline temperature implementation, search ranges and a 100-epoch baseline versus 50+50-epoch VQEL schedule; v1 provided only an illustrative equal-budget example. However, v2 removes v1's EMA decay, stale-code threshold, selected commitment weights, 100-step reward-baseline description and validation-checkpoint selection rule. Reproducibility documentation therefore changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands and reframes the motivation around Language of Thought and Inner Speech, adding Fodor and Alderson-Day–Fernyhough alongside newer emergent-language and evaluation literature. General linguistic references used in v1 disappear. Its comparison with Carmeli et al. also changes: v2 describes inference-only quantization, omitting v1's acknowledgment of their training-and-inference quantization setting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and emergent-language related work are extensively rewritten. V2 reorganizes the method into numbered module subsections and pseudocode, separates experimental setup from results, and structures results around agent roles with two appendices. Terminology changes from Text to Message modules, and the title and author information are revised.

P2.justification: V1's separate architecture diagrams are merged and redrawn as v2 Figure 1, and a new generator/codebook diagram appears as Figure 2. Dataset-specific accuracy tables become tables organized around training variants and multiple metrics; candidate-count curves are added, the unique-message chart is revised, and sensitivity plots disappear. The page template and text width also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses two important weaknesses in v1: the absence of an evaluated Gumbel-Softmax comparator and the inability to distinguish self-play's contribution from VQ architecture alone. The added baseline and Table 3 control substantially strengthen the central empirical argument, while Appendix B documents a useful failure boundary. Removed hyperparameter details and sensitivity studies, together with conclusion-level generalizations broader than the reported successes, remain material drawbacks. Nevertheless, the new comparisons and controls make the main contribution substantially better supported and assessable.
